Total Rewards of a Allied Health Professional The primary purpose of the position is to facilitate access to appropriate VA and community-based services, promote stabilization, and reduce risk of homelessness and recidivism.

The VJP Specialist works in partnership with criminal justice agencies, community organizations, and VA clinical programs to support successful community reintegration. The VJP Specialist is licensed at the independent practice level and practices within professional scope.

While capable of diagnostic formulation within scope of practice, the primary focus of the role is outreach, engagement, coordination, and facilitation of care rather than serving as a primary outpatient psychotherapist.

Ongoing clinical treatment responsibility transfers to receiving VA programs once the Veteran is engaged in care, consistent with VHA Directive 1110.04(1), Integrated Case Management Standards of Practice.

The incumbent is administratively responsible for daily operation of the VJP program, data management, and compliance with national program monitoring requirements. Outreach and Engagement: The incumbent conducts active outreach to justice-involved Veterans in jails, prisons, courts, and community supervision settings.

Outreach activities include field interviews, identification of Veterans through approved processes, coordination with correctional staff, and provision of education regarding VA services.

The VJP Specialist establishes and maintains professional relationships with judges, officers of the court, probation and parole officers, correctional administrators, law enforcement agencies, and community partners to ensure access to justice-involved Veterans and continuity of care.

Clinical Assessment and Treatment-Matching: The incumbent conducts psychosocial treatment-matching assessments to identify biopsychosocial needs and determine appropriate referrals to VA and community-based services.

Responsibilities include: - Assessing risk factors, acuity, and stabilization needs. - Developing individualized referral and engagement plans. - Facilitating linkage to medical, mental health, substance use disorder, housing, employment, peer support, and other supportive services. - Providing consultation regarding engagement strategies and clinical needs.

Clinical services provided within this role are focused on engagement, assessment, and coordination. Ongoing specialty mental health treatment is provided by receiving VA clinical programs once engagement is established. Duties are continued in the education section.

The Social Worker serves as a full-time member of the Behavioral Health Interdisciplinary Program (BHIP) within the Mental Health ICC at the Syracuse VA Medical Center.

This position provides outpatient mental health services to Veterans connected with the Syracuse VAMC and its Community-Based Outpatient Clinics (CBOCs) and is based at the Oswego VA CBOC. The Syracuse VAMC is a large, complexity level 1C facility serving Veterans, families, and caregivers across thirteen counties, including seven CBOCs.

As an affiliated tertiary care system, it offers a broad range of specialized programs. Primary responsibilities include delivering psychiatric interventions, mental health treatment, and stabilization services in an outpatient setting.

The Social Worker provides recovery-oriented, trauma-informed psychotherapy for individuals and couples, conducts psychosocial assessments, crisis interventions, and treatment planning, and employs measurement-based care and other evidence-based practices. Group therapy may be facilitated as needed.

Services are delivered both in person and via telehealth to ensure access to care. Collaboration with Veterans, caregivers, and interdisciplinary team members is essential to providing comprehensive mental health services.

The Social Worker is required to maintain an unrestricted clinical license and adhere to the NASW Code of Ethics and all applicable local Social Work policies.

Major Duties and Responsibilities, include but are not limited to: - Provide individual and couple psychotherapy using evidence-based, recovery-focused, and trauma-informed approaches. - Complete psychosocial assessments and collaboratively develop treatment plans using Measurement Based Care. - Apply knowledge of psychiatric conditions, evidence-based treatment protocols (including CBT and CPT), and common psychotropic medications, including their effects and side effects. - Use appropriate mental health and medical diagnostic terminology to maintain clear, effective communication with the healthcare team. - Participate in collaborative clinical discussions and advocate for Veterans' psychosocial and mental health needs, including factors influencing treatment adherence. - Routinely assess Veterans' mental health needs in outpatient settings, coordinate care with the clinical team, and support smooth transitions to the least restrictive level of care, including timely discharge and transition planning. - Document all clinical services in the electronic health record and review provider notes to ensure coordinated, comprehensive care. - Conduct rapid assessments and develop crisis management plans, including evaluation for psychiatric hospitalization or residential program admission. - Have some basic knowledge of Veteran benefits, services, and specialized programs. - Perform additional duties as assigned to support service and organizational needs. - Engage in ongoing professional development through self-assessment, supervision, and clinical consultation.
